transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-12-04
Start: 15:00 PST
Duration: ~45m
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Jonas Park (Redwood SE), Lena Ortiz (AetherGrid Head of Partnerships), Samir Das (AetherGrid Cloud Solutions), Priya Nair (BizDev), Marco Villa (Edge Ops)

[00:00] Maya Chen: Hi everyone, thanks for joining, we really appreciate the intro. I'm Maya, AE on the partnerships team here at Redwood. Jonas is our solutions engineer. Could we do a quick round of intros?
[00:15] Lena Ortiz: Sure, I'm Lena, head of partnerships at AetherGrid, we run a regional GPU marketplace and also provide private racks for edge customers. Samir?
[00:25] Samir Das: Hey all, Samir, cloud solutions architect. I manage our fleet deployment and API surface.
[00:32] Priya Nair: Priya, biz dev. We're exploring channels and potential integrations.
[00:37] Jonas Park: Quick hello from me, Jonas, SE. I'll try to keep technical questions sharp.
[00:44] Maya Chen: Great. High level — Redwood provides hosted inference, dedicated reserved capacity, and private deployments with a unified control plane. Today hoping to learn about AetherGrid's offering and explore where a partnership makes sense — marketplace integration, reseller, or private deployment references.
[01:05] Lena Ortiz: We're interested in partner integrations — customers want turnkey inference and we don't want to manage models ourselves. Two asks: 1) a smooth onboarding flow for our marketplace users, and 2) a predictable pricing / rev share model.
[01:20] Samir Das: On the infra side, we operate mixed GPUs — mostly A100/RTX-class nodes and some Ampere Next-gen; we also run smaller, latency-optimized edge racks for enterprise customers. We need to understand network requirements for private deployments and KMS support.
[01:40] Jonas Park: Thanks. On the private side Redwood supports a private control plane with VPC connectors, customer-managed networking, and KMS/HSM integrations. For on-prem we can do an air-gapped installer with manual KMS configs. There are some variations depending on whether customers choose Dedicated or Private.
[02:02] Maya Chen: Quick qualification — what are example workloads? Are customers doing chat, embeddings, streaming inference?
[02:12] Marco Villa: Mostly chat and low-latency reranking for search at the edge. Some customers also need embeddings for vector search but they care about token costs.
[02:24] Maya Chen: Makes sense — we typically recommend smaller quantized models for embeddings to save cost, and for chat you can pick a variant based on latency targets. Jonas, can you speak to quantization and model variants?
[02:36] Jonas Park: Yeah, our runtime supports quantized variants and selects kernels based on model arch and sequence length. For edge racks with limited memory we recommend 4-bit quant models for 7B/13B sizes or sharded 70B single-node with batching disabled — but that depends on GPU memory. Our runtime also has prefix/KV caching to help warm contexts.
[03:00] Samir Das: On network — enterprises require private peering and SSO. We use SAML for customer auth and expect audit logs. Is Redwood able to push logs to our SIEM?
[03:12] Maya Chen: Yes — we have audit logs and can stream to a customer's SIEM via syslog or S3 export. We support SAML SSO and RBAC for team-level access; SOC 2 is in place. We also support customer-managed KMS integrations.
[03:30] Lena Ortiz: Pricing is critical for the marketplace — customers will compare per-token costs. What levers do you expose? Batching, caching, quantization?
[03:42] Jonas Park: Exactly. From the infra side, batching helps throughput but increases tail latency; caching reduces token generation for repeated prompts. We also have quantization profiles and suggestions in Redwood Optimize to pick the best tradeoff. For marketplace agreements we could look at per-inference pricing plus a reseller margin.
[04:05] Priya Nair: For partner program — do you have a standard rev-share or referral? Any minimum commitments?
[04:12] Maya Chen: We have flexible models — self-serve referrals, and for deeply integrated partners we negotiate revenue share or committed capacity contracts. For Dedicated/Private customers we often do reserved commits. Lena, we can send the partner program doc with options.
[04:28] Samir Das: A couple technical Qs — can Redwood run in environments where we control the networking, e.g., peered VPCs and customer-owned load balancers? And what's the path for kernel-level optimizations for unusual GPUs?
[04:42] Jonas Park: You can definitely run in customer-controlled VPCs; we support sidecars and a private control plane. For kernel optimizations, our runtime has a kernel selector and we can work with partners to add optimized kernels for custom hardware; that usually needs SE engagement and bench runs.
[05:00] Maya Chen: Thinking about a pilot — a two-month POC where we run a 7B chat model on one of your edge racks and a 13B model on a central rack, measure latency and cost, and iterate. Does that sound reasonable?
[05:14] Marco Villa: Yes, that aligns with what our customers want. We can provision two racks for a pilot.
[05:20] Lena Ortiz: Success criteria: sub-200ms p95 for edge chat, less than 3x cost vs our baseline, and smooth onboarding for our marketplace users.
[05:31] Jonas Park: Noted. For p95 under 200ms we need to tune batching and caching aggressively. We'll propose a config and run small bench tests.
[05:44] Samir Das: What about model provenance — some customers demand model lineage and fine-tune tracking. Do you provide model versioning and rollout controls?
[05:55] Maya Chen: Yes — Redwood provides model cataloging, rollout policies (canary, A/B), and eval hooks to detect regressions. We can tie quality monitoring to prompt sets.
[06:07] Priya Nair: On legal/compliance — can we surface standard SOC2/ISO docs for potential joint customers?
[06:13] Maya Chen: We'll include SOC2 and our standard security docs in the packet. Also any additional compliance needs can be discussed; we support customer-managed audit logs and KMS.
[06:26] Lena Ortiz: Are you seeing other partners building a reseller marketplace? Any competitors we should be aware of for reference partnerships?
[06:34] Maya Chen: Some partners work with cloud vendors and hardware vendors — we've seen conversations with Velascale, Aurora, and some direct integrations with NVIDIA NGC. We can share partner playbooks.
[06:50] Samir Das: On the integration side, what is the expected engineering lift to enable provisioning from our marketplace dashboard to trigger a Redwood private deployment?
[06:59] Jonas Park: Depends on automation level. Minimal: webhook -> provisioning -> operator-led install, maybe 2–4 engineer-weeks. Fully automated (self-serve) with VPC peering, automated keys, and billing hooks might be 6–10 engineer-weeks. We can scope a phased approach.
[07:20] Maya Chen: Good to call out phased approach — pilot manual, then automation in phase two.
[07:28] Lena Ortiz: Do you have any references where Redwood ran in partner hardware?
[07:33] Maya Chen: We have a few dedicated customers and one private on-prem partner reference in EMEA; we can share anonymized metrics. I'll include a case study link.
[07:44] Marco Villa: Network latency numbers will be important — our edge racks often see higher jitter. How tolerant is Redwood to jitter?
[07:53] Jonas Park: Our runtime is tolerant; we recommend local batching and shorter sequences. Also using short-lived KV caches and local inference reduces back-and-forth. We'll recommend a config for jitter-prone networks.
[08:12] Samir Das: For KMS/HSM — does Redwood integrate with AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and customer HSMs?
[08:19] Maya Chen: Yes — AWS/GCP KMS supported, and we have partners for HSM integration. For fully air-gapped installs we can do manual key material injection.
[08:30] Priya Nair: Commercially, what's your baseline pricing for Dedicated racks and for Private installs? Ballpark to evaluate margins.
[08:38] Maya Chen: Ballpark numbers: Dedicated reserved capacity pricing depends on GPU type — for A100-class maybe $X/hr/node reserved, private installs have a platform fee plus per-node charges. I'll send the exact pricing sheet; we can discuss rev-share models after you review.
[08:55] Lena Ortiz: For the marketplace flow, we'd like an embedded checkout where when customers click "deploy" we trigger provisioning. Are redwood APIs idempotent for retry?
[09:04] Jonas Park: Our APIs are idempotent for provisioning; we also expose webhook events for lifecycle updates. We can provide a developer sandbox to prototype.
[09:18] Samir Das: Would you be willing to run an initial benchmark on one of our Ampere Next-gen nodes to validate perf?
[09:25] Jonas Park: Yes, we'll run bench tests. We'll need an SSH access or telemetry bundle to replicate conditions. For a quick bench we can also push a small container.
[09:38] Maya Chen: Recap of action items and next steps: we'll send partner deck + pricing, Jonas will prepare a latency/cost matrix, Samir will share infra spec, and we'll schedule a technical deep-dive the week of 12/14. Does that sound right?
[09:52] Lena Ortiz: Yup, sounds good.
[09:56] Priya Nair: One more Q — marketplace customers often want usage-based cancellation and data-retention controls. Is data retention adjustable per customer?
[10:05] Maya Chen: Yes — retention policies are configurable and we can apply customer-level retention/eviction policies. We also support per-account data isolation.
[10:18] Marco Villa: On observability — what metrics will you expose so we can surface to our dashboard?
[10:24] Jonas Park: Latency percentiles (p50/p95/p99), tokens per second, error rates, cost per token estimates, and trace IDs. All can be pulled into your dashboards via APIs or pushed via webhooks.
[10:38] Samir Das: Any limitations on model licenses we should be aware of if we host open models on our racks?
[10:45] Maya Chen: Model licensing varies by model; many open models allow inference but restrict redistribution. We handle licensing guidance in onboarding and will flag models with constraints.
[10:59] Lena Ortiz: OK — sounds like a promising fit. We'll review docs when we get them and align legal on the partner terms.
[11:07] Maya Chen: Great — we'll follow up with the packet. Thanks everyone for your time.
[11:15] Meeting end.

Notes: transcript contains typical transcription artifacts; some proper nouns may be mis-heard (e.g., Ampere Next-gen, product names). Links referenced in next steps will be shared in the follow-up email.
